messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "The quiet ones are getting ready — not panicking, just packing essentials, checking routes. It’s not about fear anymore, it’s about timing. Let’s keep our heads down, stay sharp, and be ready to move when the silence gets louder."
Sender 2: "The air feels different—people are talking, even the quiet ones. I’ve heard whispers, seen shifts in the way things are run. Something’s breaking, but I don’t know if it’s the regime or the silence around it. Be careful. Watch the details."
Sender 3: "Just a heads-up—things feel… off. I’ve been hearing the same quiet stories from a few people I trust: the usual routines are breaking down, and no one’s pretending otherwise anymore. Best to keep our heads down and stay in touch only when safe."
Sender 4: "The weather’s been strange lately—warm in March, then sudden cold. My cousin still hasn’t called, and the news feels… off. Like the usual silence is louder than before."
Sender 5: "The air’s different lately — even the usual silence feels lighter. I’ve heard whispers from a few trusted corners, and the way things are moving, it’s like everyone’s holding their breath but also… ready. Just keep your head down, stay sharp, and don’t say more than you need to."
Sender 6: "Just heard the baker’s son is leaving for the border next week — says his family’s been packing for weeks. Seems like everyone’s quietly making plans, even the ones who used to talk about loyalty. Be careful what you say, especially on calls."
Sender 7: "Just got word from a reliable source — the permits for the new housing project are still stuck in limbo, and it’s not just one office, it’s every one we’ve checked. Feels like the usual delays, but this time… no one’s even pretending to be in charge. Don’t talk about it, but maybe start keeping things in order."
Sender 8: "The tea at the corner house has been getting stronger lately—everyone’s talking, and not just about the weather. Just keep an eye on the streets, and don’t leave your spare keys out."
Sender 9: "Just got back from the market—everything’s quiet, people are laughing, kids running around like nothing’s changed. My friend handed me a book yesterday and said, “Nothing’s happening worth worrying about,” which, honestly, felt like the most loaded thing I’ve heard in months."
Sender 10: "The streets feel different — people are speaking openly, even joking, and the usual silence is gone. Something’s shifting, and it’s not just in our heads. We should be ready, but careful."

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 10 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 10.
